cards.name: SqaureFountain
cards.summary: Transparency preset read from <CorelDRAW 2024 install folder>/Custom Data/Transparency.cdss (a JSON style sheet); the preset name is spelled 'SqaureFountain' in the file. The file stores fill type 2 (fountain) with fountainType 4 (square), primaryAlpha 206, secondaryAlpha 84, no intermediate colours and 256 steps; if alpha is read as opacity, that is about 81 percent opaque to about 33 percent opaque. The thumbnail is a script render of the preset on a solid orange rectangle over a light grey and white checkerboard: a pale, almost clear square-shaped glow in the middle grows out to stronger orange at the edges and corners, like the radial preset with squarer contours.
use_for: a square window or spotlight in an overlay
square-edged vignettes and frames
tints that clear toward the middle of a panel
avoid: A round fade: use RadialFountain; the square type keeps the glow square.
Typing the name in a script: the file spells it SqaureFountain, so a lookup for SquareFountain finds nothing.
cards.applies_to: a vector object or bitmap (the batch requires 'vector object or bitmap'): the preset sets the whole object's transparency
cards.how_to_apply: Select the object, then use the Transparency tool or Object Properties > Transparency, choose fountain, type square, start 206 and end 84 alpha (or the matching percentages). Script: Shape.Transparency.ApplyFountainTransparency(Start, End, cdrSquareFountainFill, ...) with values converted from the file's alpha values; the thumbnail was made from this preset's file values (the harvest did not locate a preset list in the interface).

verified.note: Script render matches: a pale, nearly clear square-contoured centre growing to stronger orange at the edges and corners; type 2, fountainType 4, alphas 206/84 and 256 steps match Transparency.cdss.

review.changes: summary: checkerboard described as light grey and white (measured)

cards.name: patterns
cards.summary: Two-colour pattern library file (patterns.bpt in <CorelDRAW 2024 install folder>/Custom Data), decoded from the file: it stores exactly 39 patterns, each a 1-bit black-and-white bitmap (4 of 16 px, 9 of 32 px, 4 of 64 px, 8 of 128 px and 14 of 256 px, square). The app recolours the black and white with the fill's front and back colours. In file order the decoded patterns are: a large disc with corner quarter-discs, a check, a plus-shaped grid, a brick wall, vertical stripes, grouped horizontal and vertical lines, thin diagonal lines, a ring, a dotted diagonal band, a wavy dotted line, a baluster (vase-and-bar) outline, three curved dotted-line patterns, corner brackets (nested L lines), dotted concentric arcs, squares in perspective, nested squares, an octagon, a hexagon mesh, scalloped wavy lines, plaiting, a star, a star-and-diamond tile, a maple leaf, the four card suits (diamond, heart, spade, club), a flower, a bold X, basket-weave blocks, a box outline, a big thin X, a second check, two diagonal hatchings, a diamond mesh and a key-pattern frame; the four 16 px tiles (the two checks, the plus grid and the box outline) hold their motif in the lower half under a solid black upper half with a few stray white pixels. The thumbnail is a script render of 12 of them as two-colour fills on 12 squares (canvas 1 to 12): a dot grid, curved lines, a plain tile, a tile with a black right edge, two vertical bars, two horizontal bars, a thin diagonal, two black quarter-circles, a plain tile, another plain tile and a thick frame; several squares look empty because the pattern tiles are larger than the square, so the squares show only a corner of them.
use_for: simple repeating backgrounds in two colours of your choice
stripes, checks, bricks, weaves and motif tiles for packaging and textiles
retro, hatched and print-friendly fills that separate cleanly
avoid: Photographic or shaded textures: every pattern is pure two-tone, so there are no gradients.
Trusting the thumbnail: several of the 12 sample squares look blank because only a corner of a larger tile shows; the library has 39 patterns.
Fine detail at a small size: the 16 px and 32 px tiles repeat quickly and can look busy; the 256 px tiles repeat slowly.
cards.applies_to: a closed vector shape's fill (the batch requires 'vector object (fill)'): the library supplies the pattern bitmaps for the Two-colour pattern fill
cards.how_to_apply: Select a closed shape, open the Interactive Fill tool or Object Properties > Fill, choose Two-colour pattern fill and pick a tile, then set the front and back colours. Script: Shape.Fill.ApplyPatternFill(cdrTwoColorPattern, , PatternCanvasIndex, FrontColor, EndColor) (type-library signature; the thumbnail used canvas indexes 1 to 12, and which index maps to which of the 39 decoded patterns was not checked). File: <CorelDRAW 2024 install folder>/Custom Data/patterns.bpt (binary, decoded).

verified.note: Thumbnail matches (12 two-colour squares: dot grid, curves, plain tiles, bars, diagonal, quarter-circles, frame), and patterns.bpt decodes to 39 1-bit DIBs (4x16, 9x32, 4x64, 8x128, 14x256 px) as stated, but the motif list had no 1 x 1 check, one flower not two, two hatchings not three, and missed the baluster and star-and-diamond tiles.

review.changes: summary: motif list rewritten in file order from the decoded patterns.bpt (uint16 count, uint32 offsets, BITMAPINFOHEADER + 2-colour palette per entry): no 1 x 1 check, one flower, two hatchings, baluster and star-and-diamond tiles added, odd 16 px tiles noted; look 'card suits and flowers' -> 'card suits and a flower'
